title: Steak Quesadilla
subtitle: Sliced ribeye steak with peppers and cheese in a toasted flour tortilla
excerpt: Thinly sliced ribeye steak cooked fast in a very hot pan with cumin and smoked paprika, then sandwiched with cheddar and sautéed peppers between two toasted flour tortillas.
sourceNotes: Steak quesadillas: a premium Tex-Mex restaurant dish widely made at home across the American Southwest. The ribeye steak used here substitutes for the traditional beef skirt (arrachera), which is not widely available in the UK.

content.text: Steak quesadillas use fast-cooked, thinly sliced ribeye steak and sautéed peppers layered with cheddar between two toasted flour tortillas. Ribeye has enough fat to stay juicy at high heat; a very hot pan cooks the thin slices in under 2 minutes. Rest the steak before slicing so the juices redistribute, then cut into strips before filling.

items.prepNote: one ribeye steak, about 1.5 cm thick

content.text: A cast-iron skillet gets hotter than most frying pans and gives the steak better colour. The sautéed peppers can cook in a separate frying pan at the same time.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add the red and green peppers and the cumin. Cook for a further 4-5 minutes until the peppers are soft and lightly charred at the edges. Season with salt. Set aside.

Rub the ribeye with the cumin, smoked paprika, {{vegetable-oil}} of oil, and salt. Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Cook the steak for 2-3 minutes on each side for medium. Rest on a board for 3 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.

Wipe the cast-iron skillet clean and return to medium heat. Lay one flour tortilla flat, scatter with cheese, then add half the steak strips and half the pepper mixture. Top with another tortilla. Cook 2 minutes until the base is golden; flip carefully and cook 1.5-2 minutes. Rest 1 minute on a board, then cut into wedges.
Repeat with the remaining ingredients. Serve with soured cream and sliced jalapeño.

items.cause: Not rested before slicing, or sliced with the grain rather than against it
items.fix: Rest the steak for at least 3 minutes. Slice across the grain, not along it; across-grain slices cut short muscle fibres and are much more tender.

items.symptom: Peppers are still raw when the steak is ready
items.fix: Start the peppers first as they take longer; the steak cooks in under 6 minutes total. Both should be ready at the same time if the peppers go on first.

items.symptom: Quesadilla is soggy with juice from the steak
items.cause: Steak sliced too soon and still running with juices
items.fix: Rest the steak fully before slicing. Drain any excess juice from the steak strips on a board before filling.

items.cause: Uneven heat in the pan, or quesadilla not pressed flat
items.fix: Press gently with a spatula as it cooks. Cast iron distributes heat more evenly than thin pans.

content.text: Steak quesadillas are a step up from the chicken version in a Tex-Mex meal: richer, more substantial, and suited to an evening meal rather than lunch. In Mexico, arrachera (skirt steak) is the traditional cut used in quesadillas and fajitas because of its rich flavour and quick cooking. Ribeye is the closest substitute widely available in the UK; it has similar marbling and cooks well at high heat.
